title: Do Vision Foundation Models Enhance Domain Generalization in Medical Image Segmentation?
mechanism: Frozen VFM (DINOv2, SAM, MAE) tuned with Rein / Rein-LoRA / Ladder plus a strong decoder head; VFMs match CNNs in-domain but generalise much better to unseen scanners.
evidence: R (full text): 10 to 198 training volumes, greyscale MRI/CT. DINOv2 + Rein-LoRA DG Dice: brain 52-55 vs 44 for ResNet101-UNet; lumbar spine 31-41 vs 1-6 for U-Nets; in-domain about equal. Larger VFMs help DG slightly, not ID.
adaptation: Use as a side branch on the house PF U-Net++ R34 (VFM-H): frozen DINOv2-L at 1024 px (grey to 3 channels) with Rein-LoRA, features added at stride 16/32 decoder inputs; house keeps the 1-2 px crack path. Target E1 (half-cut, scuff), plus leave-BMRK-out as a source-shift probe.
min_experiment: Arm VFM-H (DINOv2-L + Rein-LoRA) vs house PF; module-grouped 5-fold CV + one E1 opening; metric E1 crack relF1@2 and E1 inactive IoU, CV crack relF1@2; kill if CV relF1@2 drops >0.005 AND E1 relF1@2 not +0.03 over about 0.42 AND E1 inactive IoU not above 0.24.
prior_overlap: Section 5 foundation row tested only linear probes and a 4k-step ConvNeXt-T PF screen; no PEFT, no ViT-L, never judged on E1. Open.

alt_notes.adaptation: Use its ranking of VFM + PEFT pairs to pick VFM-H's backbone and tuning method before spending GPU time; the 5-source plus E1 split is our analogue of multi-site DG.
alt_notes.min_experiment: No own arm: read the full text (open access) and choose the two VFM + PEFT pairs it ranks best for VFM-H; kill this item if its best pair is not one we already plan.

alt_notes.adaptation: Template for our E1 study: same PEFT x head grid, our 5 sources as domains (leave-one-source-out), E1 as the external domain.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Leave-one-source-out CV over the 5 sources for house vs best FM arm; metric held-out-source crack relF1@2; kill if mean gain < 0.02.
